children: Radico Khaitan shares on Friday snapped their previous session's decline and settled higher after brokerage JM Financial retained its 'Buy' rating on the stock, seeing up to 16 percent upside potential.
Shares of the company settled at Rs 4,535.10 per share on the NSE, up 1.2 percent. Earlier in the day, it made a high of Rs 4,600 per share, up 2.63 percent.
In a note, the brokerage said Radico Khaitan had a healthy start to FY27 and expected sales growth to remain strong in the premium and above (P&A) segment, outperforming peers.
"The vodka category is seeing robust traction in India and the story here is far from over. Radico remains the dominant leader and we see enough headroom for growth," JM Financial said.
The brokerage estimated more than 20 percent volume CAGR for Radico Khaitan's vodka business between FY26 and FY29, despite rising competition.
It said rising acceptance of white spirits, a wide portfolio, innovation, including flavour-based launches, and strong growth in key markets such as Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan would support growth.
Recovery in 8PM Premium Black, sustained momentum in After Dark and expansion of the luxury portfolio through distribution in hotel chains and travel retail are other key revenue drivers, it said.
The brokerage expects 8PM Premium Black to grow 20-25 percent following its relaunch with new packaging, while After Dark is expected to benefit from its packaging revamp and entry into Telangana.

On raw materials, JM Financial said extra neutral alcohol (ENA) and packaging costs remained inflationary. However, it expects Radico Khaitan to manage the impact through a better product mix, benefits from the UK-FTA and some inventory gains.
"Overall, we do not see any challenges to its FY27 guidance (of P&A volume growth of 25 percent and EBITDA margin of 20 percent) and earnings visibility is intact," the brokerage said.
JM Financial rolled forward its estimates to September 2028 and raised its target price to Rs 5,190 from Rs 4,955, while retaining its 'Buy' rating.

Radico Khaitan expects more than 25 percent value growth in its luxury portfolio, driven by innovation and expansion of distribution. Royal Ranthambore is expected to be the key contributor, followed by Rampur Single Malt and Jaisalmer Gin.
The brokerage expects a compounded annual sales growth of 25 percent for Radico Khaitan's premium portfolio between FY26 and FY29.
It said inflation in extra neutral alcohol and container costs remained a concern, but expects the company to navigate these challenges and achieve an EBITDA margin of 20 percent in FY27.
